# Gradle

> GradleはJVM系プロジェクト向けのオープンソースビルド自動化ツールで、柔軟な依存関係管理・マルチプロジェクトビルド・Maven/Ivy公開をGroovy/Kotlin DSLで開発者に提供する。

## Getting Started

- [Publishing a project as module](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/publishing_setup.adoc): The vast majority of software projects build something that aims to be consumed in some way.

## Guide

- [Policy on AI-Assisted Contributions to the Gradle Build Tool](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/AI_POLICY.md): We use AI tools daily and welcome AI-assisted contributions—provided the human behind them meets the standards below.
- [Build execution model](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/build-execution-model.md): At the highest level, Gradle's execution model is quite simple:
- [Build state model](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/build-state-model.md): The Gradle daemon tracks state for various elements.
- [Gradle platform architecture](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/platforms.md): Gradle is arranged into coarse-grained components called "architecture modules" and "platforms".
- [Gradle runtimes](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/runtimes.md): Gradle is made up of the following processes that work together to "run the build":

- [ADR-0005 - Introduce a UI architecture module to the core platform](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/standards/0005-introduce-core-ui-architecture-module.md): - ACCEPTED on 2024-02-07
- [ADR-0006 - Use of Provider APIs in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/standards/0006-use-of-provider-apis-in-gradle.md): - ACCEPTED on 2024-06-21
- [ADR-0007 - Support running Gradle on multiple Java versions and do not embed a Java runtime in the Gradle distribution](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/standards/0007-java-pre-requisite.md): - PROPOSED on 2024-12-20

- [Error messages and suggestions](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/contributing/ErrorMessages.md): Traditionally, if an error occurred, the error message and the possible solution were provided to the console via a single String in the corresponding exception.

- [Tracking down performance regressions with `git bisect`](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/testing/performance/docs/performance-bisect.md): When you see a performance regression, either by looking at the performance graph or by having a new failing test, given the current slow feedback cycle, it can be difficult to track the exact commit that triggered the regression.
- [Best Practices for Authoring Gradle Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices.adoc): Gradle is a powerful and flexible tool for building software, but along with these benefits comes complexity and the need for clear guidance on best practices.
- [Best Practices for Dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_dependencies.adoc): Version Catalogs provide a centralized, declarative way to manage dependency versions throughout a build.
- [General Gradle Best Practices](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_general.adoc): Prefer the Kotlin DSL (build.gradle.kts) over the Groovy DSL (build.gradle) when authoring new builds or creating new subprojects in existing builds.
- [Best Practices Index](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_index.adoc): The table below provides a complete list of documented Gradle Best Practices.
- [Best Practices for Performance](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_performance.adoc): Gradle publishes two distribution variants for each release: -bin (binaries only) and -all (binaries, sources, and documentation).
- [Best Practices for Structuring Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_structuring_builds.adoc): Modularize your builds by splitting your code into multiple projects.
- [Best Practices for Tasks](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_tasks.adoc): The task dependsOn method should only be used for <<organizingtasks.adoc#sec:lifecycletasks,lifecycle tasks>> (tasks without task actions).
- [Best Practices for Testing](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_testing.adoc): You should test any custom tasks or plugins you create using <<testkit.adoc#testkit,Gradle TestKit>>.
- [Gradle Build Lifecycle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/build_lifecycle_intermediate.adoc): The build lifecycle is the sequence of phases Gradle executes to turn your build scripts, source code, and more, into completed work.
- [Declaring and Managing Dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/dependencies_intermediate.adoc): Gradle provides a rich and flexible model for declaring dependencies, managing versions, and resolving conflicts across builds.
- [Anatomy of a Gradle Build](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/gradle_directories_intermediate.adoc): A Gradle build is made up of several key components that work together to automate tasks like compiling code, running tests, and packaging artifacts.
- [Gradle Managed Types](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/gradle_managed_types_intermediate.adoc): Gradle Managed Types are the building blocks for writing modern, efficient, and cache-friendly build logic.
- [Structuring Multi-Project Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/multi_project_builds_intermediate.adoc): As your codebase grows, organizing it into multiple subprojects becomes essential for maintainability, performance, and reuse.
- [Working with Plugins](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/plugins_intermediate.adoc): Much of Gradle's functionality is delivered via plugins, including core plugins distributed with Gradle, third-party plugins, and custom plugins defined within builds.
- [Writing Build Scripts](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/writing_build_scripts_intermediate.adoc): The initialization phase in the Gradle Build lifecycle finds the settings file.
- [Creating and Registering Tasks](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/authoring-builds/writing_tasks_intermediate.adoc): The work that Gradle can do on a project is defined by one or more tasks.
- [Binary Plugin](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/developing-plugins/binary_plugin_advanced.adoc): Creating your own custom plugin might be a great solution when Gradle doesn't offer the specific capabilities your project needs.
- [Binary Plugin Development](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/developing-plugins/developing_binary_plugin_advanced.adoc): When creating a plugin in Gradle, you will most likely offer tasks users can run and DSL blocks that users can use to configure your plugin.
- [Plugin Introduction](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/developing-plugins/plugin_introduction_advanced.adoc): A Gradle plugin is an add-on that enhances your build by adding tasks, applying conventions, or enabling specific configurations.
- [Pre-compiled Script Plugins](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/developing-plugins/pre_compiled_script_plugin_advanced.adoc): The simplest plugin you can develop is called a precompiled script plugins.
- [Binary Plugin Publishing](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/developing-plugins/publishing_binary_plugin_advanced.adoc): Once your plugin is complete and tested, you may want to publish it so it can be reused across multiple builds or even shared with others.
- [Binary Plugin Testing](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/developing-plugins/testing_binary_plugin_advanced.adoc): Gradle provides a robust mechanism for testing binary plugins.
- [Build File Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/build_file_basics.adoc): Generally, a build script (build.gradle(.kts)) details build configuration, tasks, and plugins.
- [Build Scan Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/build_scans.adoc): A Build Scan is a representation of metadata captured as you run your build.
- [Command-Line Interface Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/command_line_interface_basics.adoc): The command-line interface is the primary *method of interacting with Gradle* outside the IDE.
- [Dependencies and Dependency Management Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/dependency_management_basics.adoc): Gradle has built-in support for dependency management.
- [Core Concepts](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/gradle_basics.adoc): Gradle automates building, testing, and deployment of software from information in build scripts.
- [Incremental Builds and Build Caching Basic](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/gradle_optimizations.adoc): Gradle uses two main features to reduce build time: incremental builds and build caching.
- [Wrapper Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/gradle_wrapper_basics.adoc): The *recommended way to execute any Gradle build* is with the Gradle Wrapper.
- [Plugin Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/plugin_basics.adoc): Gradle is built on a flexible plugin system.
- [Settings File Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/settings_file_basics.adoc): The settings file (settings.gradle(.kts)) is the entry point of every Gradle project.
- [Task Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/fundamentals/running-builds/task_basics.adoc): A task represents some independent unit of work that a build performs, such as compiling classes, creating a JAR, generating Javadoc, or publishing archives to a repository.
- [How to Align Dependency Versions in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_align_dependency_versions.adoc): Dependency version alignment ensures that different modules belonging to the same logical group (a <<platforms.adoc#platforms,platform>>) use identical versions in the dependency graph.
- [How to Create Feature Variants for a Library in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_create_feature_variants_of_a_library.adoc): Gradle supports the concept of feature <<variant_attributes.adoc#variant-attributes,variants>>, allowing a single library to be split into multiple related but distinct modules.
- [How to Downgrade Transitive Dependencies in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_downgrade_transitive_dependencies.adoc): This guide explains how to *downgrade transitive dependencies* in Gradle when your project requires an older version due to API compatibility, bugs, or other constraints.
- [How to Exclude Transitive Dependencies in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_exclude_transitive_dependencies.adoc): This guide explains how to *exclude transitive dependencies* from your project when they are not needed or cause conflicts.
- [How to Troubleshoot Version Catalog Problems in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_fix_version_catalog_problems.adoc): Version catalogs help manage dependencies efficiently, but sometimes errors occur.
- [How to Prevent Accidental or Eager Dependency Upgrades in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_prevent_accidental_dependency_upgrades.adoc): This guide explains how to *prevent accidental dependency versions* due to Gradle's eager dependency resolution.
- [How to Resolve Specific Artifacts from a Module Dependency with Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_resolve_specific_artifacts.adoc): Gradle resolves module dependencies by looking for metadata files (.module, .pom, or ivy.xml) and a default artifact (usually a JAR).
- [How to Share Artifacts Between Projects with Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_share_outputs_between_projects.adoc): Gradle provides a mechanism to share artifacts between projects in a flexible and maintainable way using variant-aware sharing.
- [How to Upgrade Transitive Dependencies in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_upgrade_transitive_dependencies.adoc): This guide explains how to manage and upgrade versions of *transitive dependencies in Gradle using dependency constraints*.
- [How to Use a Local Fork of a Module Dependency with Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/dependency-management/how_to_use_local_forks.adoc): This guide explains how to replace a module dependency with a local fork of the module’s sources, assuming the module itself is built with Gradle.
- [How to Convert a Single-Project Build into a Multi-Project Build in Gradle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/how-to/structuring-builds/how_to_convert_single_build_to_multi_build.adoc): When your Gradle project grows, you may want to split it into multiple subprojects to improve modularity, maintainability, and parallel execution.
- [Gradle & Third-party Tools](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/integration/third_party_integration.adoc): Gradle can be integrated with many different third-party tools such as IDEs and continuous integration platforms.
- [Gradle on CircleCI](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/circleci.adoc): This page is a reference for integrating Gradle with CircleCI.
- [Gradle Docker Images](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/docker.adoc): Gradle publishes Docker Official Images for running Gradle builds inside containers.
- [Gradle on GitHub Actions](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/github-actions.adoc): This page is a reference for integrating Gradle with GitHub Actions using the official gradle/actions.
- [Gradle on GitLab CI](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/gitlab-ci.adoc): This page is a reference for integrating Gradle with GitLab CI/CD on GitLab.com, self-managed, or GitLab Dedicated instances.
- [Gradle on CI / CD Systems](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/gradle_on_ci.adoc): Gradle integrates with many Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery (CD) systems.
- [Gradle on Jenkins](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/jenkins.adoc): This page is a reference for integrating Gradle with Jenkins.
- [Gradle on TeamCity](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/teamcity.adoc): This page is a reference for integrating Gradle with JetBrains TeamCity.
- [Gradle on Travis CI](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/on-ci/travis-ci.adoc): This page is a reference for integrating Gradle with Travis CI.
- [Build Cache](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/build_cache.adoc): The Gradle build cache is a cache mechanism that aims to save time by reusing outputs produced by other builds.
- [Important concepts](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/build_cache_concepts.adoc): How much of your build gets loaded from the cache depends on many factors.
- [Debugging and diagnosing Build Cache misses](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/build_cache_debugging.adoc): To make the most of task output caching, it is important that any necessary inputs to your tasks are specified correctly, while at the same time avoiding unneeded inputs.
- [Build cache performance](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/build_cache_performance.adoc): The sole reason to use any build cache is to make builds faster.
- [Use cases for the build cache](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/build_cache_use_cases.adoc): This section covers the different use cases for Gradle’s build cache, from local-only development to caching task outputs across large teams.
- [Caching Android projects](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/caching_android_projects.adoc): While it is true that Android uses the Java toolchain as its foundation, there are nevertheless some significant differences from pure Java projects; these differences impact task cacheability.
- [Caching Java projects](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/caching_java_projects.adoc): As of Gradle 4.0, the build tool fully supports caching plain Java projects.
- [Solving common problems](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/build-cache/common_caching_problems.adoc): Small problems in a build, like forgetting to declare a configuration file as an input to your task, can be easily overlooked.
- [Configuration Cache](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/configuration-cache/configuration_cache.adoc): The Configuration Cache improves build performance by caching the result of the <<buildlifecycleintermediate.adoc#build_lifecycle,configuration phase>> and reusing it for subsequent builds.
- [Debugging and Troubleshooting the Configuration Cache](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/configuration-cache/configuration_cache_debugging.adoc): This section provides general guidelines for resolving issues with the Configuration Cache, whether in your build logic or Gradle plugins.
- [Enabling and Configuring the Configuration Cache](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/configuration-cache/configuration_cache_enabling.adoc): By default, Gradle does not use the Configuration Cache.
- [Configuration Cache Requirements for your Build Logic](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/configuration-cache/configuration_cache_requirements.adoc): To capture and reload the task graph state using the Configuration Cache, Gradle enforces specific requirements on tasks and build logic.
- [Configuration Cache Status](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/configuration-cache/configuration_cache_status.adoc): This feature is not enabled by default.
- [Isolated Projects](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/isolated_projects.adoc): Isolated Projects is an experimental feature aimed at improving Gradle scalability and performance, especially for large builds and IDE sync (Android Studio / IntelliJ IDEA).
- [Improve the Performance of Gradle Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/optimizing-builds/performance.adoc): Build performance is essential to productivity.
- [Getting Started](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/overview/getting_started.adoc): Everyone has to start somewhere, and if you're new to Gradle, this is where to begin.
- [Glossary](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/overview/glossary.adoc): The following glossary helps you understand Gradle terminology.

- [The Project Report Plugin](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/core-plugins/project_report_plugin.adoc): The Project report plugin adds some tasks to your project which generate reports containing useful information about your build.
- [Visual Studio](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/core-plugins/visual_studio_plugin.adoc): The Visual Studio Plugin generate files that are used by the Visual Studio IDE, thus making it possible to open the solution into Visual Studio (File - Open - Project/Solution...).
- [The War Plugin](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/core-plugins/war_plugin.adoc): The War plugin extends the <<javaplugin.adoc#javaplugin,Java plugin>> to add support for assembling web application WAR files.
- [Artifact Resolution](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/advanced/artifact_resolution.adoc): After constructing a dependency graph, Gradle performs artifact resolution, mapping the resolved graph to a set of artifacts that will be downloaded during the build.
- [Dependency Resolution](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/advanced/dependency_resolution.adoc): Dependency resolution in Gradle can largely be thought of as a two-step process.
- [Graph Resolution](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/advanced/graph_resolution.adoc): During the graph resolution phase, Gradle constructs a resolved dependency graph, which models the relationships between different components and their variants.
- [Variant Selection and Attribute Matching](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/advanced/variant_aware_resolution.adoc): Gradle's dependency management engine is variant aware.
- [4. Centralizing dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/basics/centralizing_dependencies.adoc): Central dependencies can be managed in Gradle using various techniques such as platforms and version catalogs.
- [1. Declaring dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/basics/declaring_dependencies.adoc): Declaring dependencies in Gradle involves specifying libraries or files that your project depends on.
- [3. Declaring repositories](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/basics/declaring_repositories.adoc): Gradle needs to know where it can download the dependencies used in the project.
- [2. Dependency Configurations](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/basics/dependency_configurations.adoc): Every dependency declared for a Gradle project applies to a specific scope.
- [5. Dependency Constraints and Conflict Resolution](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/basics/dependency_constraints_conflicts.adoc): When the same library is declared multiple times or when two different libraries provide the same functionality, a conflict can occur during dependency resolution.
- [Using Catalogs with Platforms](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/centralizing-dependencies/centralizing_catalog_platform.adoc): Both platforms and version catalogs help manage dependency versions in a project, but they serve different purposes and have different effects on depe…
- [Platforms](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/centralizing-dependencies/platforms.adoc): <script> const currentAnchor = window.location.hash.substring(1); // Remove the '#' symbol
- [Version Catalogs](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/centralizing-dependencies/version_catalogs.adoc): A version catalog is a selected list of dependencies that can be referenced in build scripts, simplifying dependency management.
- [Artifact Transforms](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/controlling-dependency-resolution/artifact_transforms.adoc): What if you want to make changes to the files contained in one of your dependencies before you use it?
- [Artifact Views](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/controlling-dependency-resolution/artifact_views.adoc): In some cases, it is desirable to customize the artifact resolution process.
- [Capabilities](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/controlling-dependency-resolution/component_capabilities.adoc): In a dependency graph, it's common for multiple implementations of the same API to be accidentally included, especially with libraries like logging frameworks where different bindings are selected by various transitive dependencies.
- [Dependency Resolution Consistency](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/controlling-dependency-resolution/dependency_resolution_consistency.adoc): In a typical Gradle project, multiple configurations exist, such as compileClasspath and runtimeClasspath.
- [Resolving Specific Artifacts](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/controlling-dependency-resolution/resolving_specific_artifacts.adoc): When resolving a module from a Maven or Ivy repository, Gradle looks for metadata (e.g., .module, pom.xml, ivy.xml) and a default artifact file (typically a JAR).
- [Variants and Attributes](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/controlling-dependency-resolution/variant_attributes.adoc): For example, a library may have an api and an implementation variant.
- [Creating Dependency Configurations](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-dependencies/declaring_configurations.adoc): In Gradle, dependencies are associated with specific scopes, such as compile-time or runtime.
- [Declaring Dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-dependencies/declaring_dependencies_basics.adoc): There are three main types of dependencies in Gradle:
- [Declaring Dependency Constraints](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-dependencies/dependency_constraints.adoc): Version declarations (including ranges) only affect the dependencies you declare directly.
- [Declaring Versions and Ranges](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-dependencies/dependency_versions.adoc): You can specify dependencies with exact versions or version ranges to define which versions your project can use:
- [Gradle distribution-specific dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-dependencies/gradle_dependencies.adoc): Gradle provides special dependency notations for projects that build Gradle plugins or tools that integrate with Gradle.
- [Viewing Dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-dependencies/viewing_debugging_dependencies.adoc): Gradle offers tools to navigate the results of dependency management, allowing you to more precisely understand how and why Gradle resolves dependencies.
- [Centralizing Repository Declarations](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-repositories/centralizing_repositories.adoc): Instead of declaring repositories in every subproject of your build or via an allprojects block, Gradle provides a way to declare them centrally for all projects.
- [Declaring Repositories Basics](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-repositories/declaring_repositories_basics.adoc): Gradle can resolve local or external dependencies from one or many repositories based on Maven, Ivy or flat directory formats.
- [Filtering Repository Content](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-repositories/filtering_repository_content.adoc): Gradle exposes an API to declare what a repository may or may not contain.
- [Metadata Formats](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-repositories/supported_metadata_formats.adoc): Dependency metadata refers to the information associated with a dependency that describes its characteristics, relationships, and requirements.
- [Supported Protocols](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-repositories/supported_repository_protocols.adoc): Gradle supports a variety of transport protocols for Maven and Ivy repositories.
- [Repository Types](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/declaring-repositories/supported_repository_types.adoc): Gradle supports various sources for resolving dependencies, accommodating different metadata formats and connectivity methods.
- [Modifying Dependency Metadata](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/dependency-management/component_metadata_rules.adoc): Each component pulled from a repository includes metadata, such as its group, name, version, and the various variants it provides along with their artifacts and dependencies.
- [Dependency Caching](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/dependency-management/dependency_caching.adoc): Gradle contains a highly sophisticated dependency caching mechanism, which seeks to minimise the number of remote requests made in dependency resolution, while striving to guarantee that the results of dependency resolution are correct and reproducible.
- [Locking Versions](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/dependency-management/dependency_locking.adoc): Using <<dependency_versions.adoc#sec:declaring-dependency-with-dynamic-version, dynamic dependency versions>> (e.g., 1.+ or [1.0,2.0)) can cause build…
- [Using Resolution Rules](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/dependency-management/resolution_rules.adoc): Gradle provides several mechanisms to directly influence the behavior of the dependency resolution engine.
- [Dependency Management](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/getting_started_dep_man.adoc): Software projects typically depend on other libraries to function.
- [Customizing publishing](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/publishing_customization.adoc): Gradle's publication model is based on the notion of components, which are defined by plugins.
- [Gradle Module Metadata](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/publishing_gradle_module_metadata.adoc): Gradle Module Metadata is a format used to serialize the Gradle component model.
- [The Ivy Publish Plugin](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/publishing_ivy.adoc): The Ivy Publish Plugin provides the ability to publish build artifacts in the Apache Ivy format, usually to a repository for consumption by other builds or projects.
- [The Maven Publish Plugin](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/publishing_maven.adoc): The Maven Publish Plugin provides the ability to publish build artifacts to an Apache Maven repository.
- [Signing artifacts](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/publishing_signing.adoc): The <<signingplugin.adoc#signingplugin, Signing Plugin>> can be used to sign all artifacts and metadata files that make up a publication, including Maven POM files and Ivy module descriptors.
- [The Signing Plugin](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dependency-management/publishing/signing_plugin.adoc): The Signing Plugin adds the ability to digitally sign built files and artifacts.
- [Default Imports](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dsl-apis/default_script_imports.adoc): To make build scripts more concise, Gradle automatically adds a set of import statements to scripts.
- [A Groovy Build Script Primer](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dsl-apis/groovy_build_script_primer.adoc): Ideally, a Groovy build script looks mostly like configuration: setting some properties of the project, configuring dependencies, declaring tasks, and so on.
- [Kotlin Dsl](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dsl-apis/kotlin_dsl.adoc): Gradle's Kotlin DSL offers an alternative to the traditional Groovy DSL, delivering an enhanced editing experience in supported IDEs with features like better content assist, refactoring, and documentation.

- [Public Gradle APIs](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/dsl-apis/public_apis.adoc): Gradle provides many public APIs that allow developers to interact with various build system components.
- [Collections](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/gradle-types/collections.adoc): Gradle provides types for maintaining collections of objects, intended to work well to extends Gradle's DSLs and provide useful features such as lazy configuration.

- [Gradle Wrapper](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/runtime-configuration/gradle_wrapper.adoc): The *recommended way to execute any Gradle build* is with the help of the Gradle Wrapper (referred to as "Wrapper").

- [Upgrading within Gradle 9.x.y](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/releases/upgrading/upgrading_version_9.adoc): This chapter provides the information you need to migrate your Gradle 9.x.y builds to the latest.
- [Verifying Dependencies](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/securing-builds/dependency_verification.adoc): Working with external dependencies and plugins from third-party repositories exposes your build to significant supply chain risks.
- [Securing Gradle Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/securing-builds/security.adoc): Every Gradle build pulls in code from external repositories, executes tools you didn’t author, and publishes artifacts that others will trust.
- [Composite Builds (Included Builds)](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/structuring-builds/composite_builds.adoc): A composite build is a build that includes other builds; those builds are known as included builds.
- [Configuration On Demand](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/structuring-builds/configuration_on_demand.adoc): Configuration-on-demand attempts to configure only the relevant projects for the requested tasks, i.e., it only evaluates the build script file of projects participating in the build.
- [Multi-Project Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/structuring-builds/multi_project_builds.adoc): As projects grow, it's common to split them into smaller, focused modules that are built, tested, and released together.
- [Structuring and Organizing Gradle Projects](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/structuring-builds/organizing_gradle_projects.adoc): It is important to structure your Gradle project to optimize build performance.
- [Sharing Build Logic using `buildSrc`](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/structuring-builds/sharing_build_logic_between_subprojects.adoc): Subprojects in a multi-project build often share common dependencies.
- [Part 1: Initializing the Project](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part1_gradle_init_project.adoc): Learn the basics of authoring Gradle by first creating a Java app using Gradle init.
- [Part 2: The Build Lifecycle](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part2_build_lifecycle.adoc): Learn about the Gradle build lifecycle and what each phase represents.
- [Part 3: Multi-Project Builds](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part3_multi_project_builds.adoc): Learn the basics of structuring Gradle projects using subprojects and composite builds.
- [Part 4: Writing the Settings File](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part4_settings_file.adoc): Learn the basics of authoring Gradle by developing the Settings File.
- [Part 5: Writing a Build Script](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part5_build_scripts.adoc): Learn the basics of authoring Gradle by developing the Build Script.
- [Part 6: Writing Tasks](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part6_writing_tasks.adoc): Learn the basics of authoring Gradle tasks by creating a simple one in your Build script.
- [Part 7: Writing Plugins](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/authoring-builds/part7_writing_plugins.adoc): Learn the basics of writing and applying Gradle plugins.
- [Part 1: Initializing the Project](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/developing-plugins/part1_gradle_init_plugin.adoc): Learn the basics of developing Gradle plugins starting with gradle init.

- [Part 4: Writing a Unit Test](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/developing-plugins/part4_unit_test.adoc): Learn the basics of unit testing your plugin to ensure it behaves as expected.
- [Part 5: Add a DataFlow Action](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/developing-plugins/part5_add_dataflow_action.adoc): Learn how to use Gradle's modern Dataflow API to hook into the build lifecycle and add an action to your plugin.
- [Part 6: Writing a Functional Test](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/developing-plugins/part6_functional_test.adoc): Learn how to write a functional test to verify your plugin's behavior in a real-world scenario.
- [Part 7: Use a Consumer Project](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/developing-plugins/part7_use_consumer_project.adoc): Learn how to set up a dummy consumer project to test your plugin without publishing it.
- [Part 8: Publish your Plugin Locally](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/tutorials/developing-plugins/part8_publish_locally.adoc): Learn how to verify your plugin can be published by pushing it to a local Maven repository, then consuming it like any external plugin.

## API Reference

- [ADR-0003 - Avoid introducing Groovy types to public API](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/architecture/standards/0003-avoid-introducing-Groovy-types-to-public-api.md): - ACCEPTED on 2024-01-12
- [Tags Used in Best Practices](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/tags_reference.adoc): Here you can find a brief explanation of all the tags used in the best practices documentation.
- [Test Event Reporting API](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/integration/test_reporting_api.adoc): The Test Event Reporting API allows you to capture test execution events programmatically and produce results similar to Gradle's built-in Test task.
- [Tooling API](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/integration/tooling_api.adoc): Gradle provides a programmatic API called the Tooling API, which you can use for embedding Gradle into your own software.
- [Gradle Plugin Reference](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/reference/core-plugins/plugin_reference.adoc): This page contains links and short descriptions for all the core plugins provided by Gradle itself.
- [Developing Parallel Tasks](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/unused/worker_api.adoc): Gradle provides an API that can split tasks into sections that can be executed in parallel.

## Optional

- [Contributing to the Gradle Build Tool](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): Thank you for your interest in contributing to Gradle!
- [Best Practices for Security](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/master/platforms/documentation/docs/src/docs/userguide/best-practices/best_practices_security.adoc): Set distributionSha256Sum in gradle-wrapper.properties to verify the integrity of the downloaded Gradle distribution.
